Deployment¶

Prism/Lente allows for various deployment strategies, and some diagrams are shown here.

Lente deployment depends on your dashboarding and Prism station management strategy. A Lente station can manage Prism stations directly below it, in the connection hierarchy.

A deployment plan should be discussed with a Sistemi support engineer.

System Requirements¶

  • Computer Minimum

    • x86, 8GB RAM, 2+ Cores

    • 256GB Storage

    • USB ports

    • Display 1900x1280

    • Laptop is recommended because it has battery backup, otherwise a UPS is recommended.

  • Host OS

    • Ubuntu 24.04

Ubuntu File System and Users¶

  • Install Ubuntu onto the computers

  • OPTIONAL: enable file system encryption

    • Note that enabling encryption will require a password to be entered for the computer to boot up. Consider this for remote sites.

      • Alternatively the home directory of the Prism/Lente account could be encrypted, which is where the Prism/Lente files will be hosted. The benefit of this approach is a password is not required to boot the computer. And the Prism/Lente files are still protected.

  • Set up at least two user accounts

    • Operator account,

      • should have very limited access

      • able to run Chrome

    • Prism/Lente Admin account

      • hosts the Prism/Lente files

Installing Prism/Lente Stations¶

Set up Lente first, then add the Prism stations. A Prism station does not need a copy of your scripts repo, it gets the scripts, drivers and license from its Lente.

  • Prism

    • Install Ubuntu and Docker per Prism Full Install (Requirements section only). Git and a clone of the scripts repo are not needed.

    • Make a folder for the Prism files, this becomes Prism’s public folder:

      mkdir -p ~/prism/public
cd ~/prism/public

    • Get the Prism helper script prism.sh from Lente. This works on networks without internet access, replace 192.168.0.10 with the IP address of your Lente:

      curl -O http://192.168.0.10:6595/prism.sh
chmod +x prism.sh

    • Copy in the settings.json for this station, see settings.json details below. The file must be supplied, Prism does not start without it.

      • site_key and prism_lente_pw must be the same as on Lente.

    • Get the Prism Docker image (needs internet access, or load the image from a file with docker load):

      docker pull sistemicorp/prismng

    • Start Prism. The script must be run from the public folder, because that folder is mounted into the Prism container. The –server flag is required, it is the IP address of the Lente this Prism reports to. Use –restart=always so Prism starts every time the computer is turned on:

      ./prism.sh --server=192.168.0.10 --restart=always start

    • On its first start Prism downloads the scripts package from Lente, installs it into public/prism, and then starts as usual. After that Lente keeps the scripts up to date, see auto_sync_scripts below.

      • If the download fails, Prism logs the reason in public/log/prism.log, also shown by docker logs prism, and exits. Usual causes are Lente not reachable, a prism_lente_pw that does not match Lente (status code 403), or a site_key that does not match Lente (decrypt failed). Fix settings.json and start Prism again.

    • For a Prism without a Lente, git clone your scripts repo and start Prism from its public folder with –server=none, as in the Prism Full Install.

  • Lente

    • install “full” per Lente Full Install HOWEVER, change the git source to be your repo.

    • Use Lente Station management to push your repo to downstream Prism (and/or Lente) computers.

    • Lente serves public/prism.sh at http://<lente>:6595/prism.sh, for setting up new Prism stations.

    • use the helper script public/lente.sh, run from the public folder, with option –restart=always so that Lente will automatically start on every computer boot up:

      cd ~/git/scripts/public
./lente.sh --restart=always start

    • the Postgres container must also be set to restart, see Postgres.

    • Optional: to let an admin update the Lente scripts from GitHub with the Station Manager git pull button, run public/git_pull_watcher.sh on the Lente host, see Lente Git Pull.

Settings.JSON File¶

  • Each Lente/Prism computer will have its own (local) settings file.

    • When setting up a new Prism/Lente instance, this file must be manually edited or copied from a reference source to reflect this instances configuration.

    • In practice, most Prism computers can use the same file, and therefore the file should be stored in a separate place and used as a source when new Prism computers are added to the deployment.

    • The settings.json in your scripts repo should only be an example. Do not commit the real deployment passwords to your repo.

  • This file is NOT propagated within the deployment by Lente.

  • This file contains passwords in plain text so it should be handled appropriately.

  • prism_lente_pw (and lente_lente_pw for Lente to Lente) must be set, and must be the same on every computer in the deployment. If they are not set, Prism/Lente refuse all station requests (pings, results, script and user syncs).

  • site_key must be set, and must be the same on every computer in the deployment. It encrypts the scripts package, the manifest, travellers and results. The demo value only works with “demo”: true. Generate a key with python3 -c “import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(24))”.

  • To check site_key, each Prism/Lente logs a site_key fingerprint at startup, which is the same on every computer when the keys match. The fingerprint does not reveal the key. The Lente Station Manager Site Key column shows Mismatch or Not set in red, and a station with a different key shows a site_key does not match Lente notice.

// This file is NOT propagated by Lente to Prism stations.
// For each Prism/Lente install, this file should be modified as required.
// See https://sistemicorp.github.io/scripts/build/html/_deployment.html#settings-json-file
{
  // turn on demo mode.  Creates test user accounts, ...
  // remove line, or set to false to disable demo mode
  "demo": true,

  // On startup optionally specify to load a traveller
  //"load_traveller": "public/traveller/traveller_TZ6T.pdf",
  //"load_user": "operator@here.com",

  // Site key, must be the same on every Prism/Lente in the deployment
  // - encrypts the scripts package, manifest, travellers and results
  // - the demo value only works with "demo": true, generate a real one with
  //   python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(24))"
  "site_key": "demo-site-key-change-me",

  // Result JSON file encryption, uses site_key
  // - a valid license file is required to encrypt results
  "result_encrypt": false,

  // By default results that are sent to Lente are backed up
  // locally, to disable this backup uncomment
  //"result_bkup_dir": null,

  // Result JSON files be backed up as encrypted, <true|false>,
  // If the results were not encrypted by Prism, they won't be ecrypted by Lente
  "results_bkup_encrypted": false,

  // Use https secure transport, requires public/cert.pem and public/key.pem files
  // For Lente & Prism stations, all must be configured the same,
  // with the same cert.pem/key.pem on every station
  "use_https": false,

  // Prism/Lente internal connection password
  "prism_lente_pw": "mysecret1",

  // Manifest (enable/disable) checking
  // Validates "public/prism" contents (sent by Lente)
  // create manifest.exclude to list file exclusions
  "manifest_check": false,

  // network interface to use, used by VPNs
  //"net_iface": "tun0",

  // Send log files on startup for diagnostic purposes
  "send_logs_on_startup": true,

  // Health checks
  // Levels: Warn, Error, Critical (case insensitive)
  // "Warn" and "Error" only appear in the notification log
  // "Critical" additionally prevents new test sessions from starting on Prism,
  // and Lente refuses result uploads
  // First rule that matches for each health check is reported
  "health_checks": {
    "disk_space": {
      "enable": true,
      "rules": [
        // free format: <value> [MB|GB|%]
        {"free": "10%",    "level": "Critical"},
        {"free": "100 MB", "level": "Error"},
        {"free": "200 MB", "level": "Warn"}
      ]
    }
  },

  // OPCUA Configuration
  "opcua_server": {
    "enable": false,
    "security_policies":[
      "NoSecurity",
      "Basic256Sha256_Sign",
      "Basic256Sha256_SignAndEncrypt"
    ],
    "certificates": {
      "enable": false,
      // "path": "public",
      // "certificate_file": "cert.pem",
      // "private_key_file": "key.pem",
    }
  },

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Below are only used by Lente and can be removed for Prism stations

  // Lente/Lente internal connection password
  "lente_lente_pw": "mysecret3",

  // Enter IP Address:port, example "http://35.123.432.190:6595"
  // Use null to disable upstream sending.
  "result_server_url": null,

  // This Lente computer is pyramid root and creates manifest
  "root_authority": true,

  // automatically sync Prism clients scripts
  "auto_sync_scripts": true,

  // maximum size (MB, uncompressed) of the scripts package sent to stations,
  // see public/prism/scripts_zip.exclude to exclude files
  //"scripts_zip_max_mb": 100,

  "postgres": {
    // resultbasekeysv1 is the name of the dB and cannot be changed
    "resultbasekeysv1": {
      // !! Change "pw" to a real password for a real deployment,
      // !! This user/pw must match your postgres deployment too,
      "user": "postgres",
      "pw": "qwerty",
      // ip address of the postgres database, use `127.0.0.1` if locahost
      "ip": "127.0.0.1"
    }
  }
}

For Prism stations, a number of items can be removed per the comments, which will make the file smaller and easier to manage.

  • see HTTPS for creating necessary files if using HTTPS feature

  • health_checks applies to Prism and Lente, see Health Checks. results_bkup_encrypted is used by Lente only

  • On Prism, result_server_url is always set from the –server flag of prism.sh

  • auto_sync_scripts also applies to Prism stations, keep it in the Prism file. When it is true on a Prism, its Lente installs new scripts on it automatically.

  • send_logs_on_startup applies to Prism and Lente. When true, the station’s log files are sent each time it starts, the same as pressing Send Logs in the Admin menu. This is useful for remote diagnostics.

    • The logs are sent as a result record, and are found in Lente Result Search under the script name PRISMSENDLOG_startup or LENTESENDLOG_startup (…_ui when sent from Send Logs). The station’s computer name is in the location field.

    • Log files larger than 1 MB are skipped, and an error notice names each skipped file.

Other Settings¶

These optional settings are not in the example file, the defaults are shown.

// seconds without activity before a logged in user is no longer reported as active,
// an active user blocks Sync Users and Sync Script to that station (Prism and Lente)
"session_inactive_timeout_s": 600,

// hours before a browser login expires and the user must log in again (Prism and Lente)
"browser_credentials_timeout_h": 168,

// Prism only: Test Portal throughput chart, seconds per bar and number of bars
"result_stats_time_bucket": 600,
"result_stats_max_buckets": 20

As noted in the comments of the settings file, this file is NOT deployed as part of the scripts synchronization that Lente does through station management. The settings file is to be configured for each computer (Lente or Prism) in the deployment.

Prism/Lente Docker Images¶

On computers that are deployed, you will want the Docker images to run (and restart) every time the computer boots up.

The helper scripts to start Prism/Lente (see Helpers), have a restart=always option that should be used. Once that is done, Prism/Lente will forever startup.

By default the helper scripts use the latest image from Docker Hub. To hold a deployment at a version, pass the image with its tag using –image= (or -i), and use the same tag on every update and start. Leaving it off any of these commands goes back to latest:

./lente.sh --image=sistemicorp/lente:v0.8.21 update
./lente.sh --image=sistemicorp/lente:v0.8.21 --restart=always start

./prism.sh --image=sistemicorp/prismng:<tag> update
./prism.sh --image=sistemicorp/prismng:<tag> --server=192.168.0.10 --restart=always start

The available tags are listed on Docker Hub. Both helper scripts also take these flags:

  • -n <number>, instance number, appended to the container name and hostname, for example -n 2 runs container lente2. Use the same number for update and stop.

  • -b, use the Docker bridge network instead of the host network.

  • -v, Lente only, start Lente with verbose logging.

Run ./lente.sh –help or ./prism.sh –help for the full list.

Lente Git Pull¶

The root Lente (“root_authority”: true) can update its scripts from GitHub with the git pull button on the Station Manager page. The button is shown to ADMIN users only. With auto_sync_scripts on, Lente then syncs the new scripts to its stations, see settings.json.

Lente runs in a Docker container that has no git access, so the pull is done on the host computer by the helper script public/git_pull_watcher.sh. The button creates the file public/.git_trigger, the watcher sees it and runs git pull in your scripts repo. The public folder is shared with the container by lente.sh, so no extra Docker setup is needed.

  • Lente refuses the pull if the watcher is not running, and refuses Sync Script while a pull is in progress.

  • The result of each pull is logged in public/.git_pull.log on the Lente host.

Setup, done once on the Lente host. The full steps, with commands and troubleshooting, are in the comments at the top of public/git_pull_watcher.sh.

  • The scripts repo remote must use SSH (git@github.com:OWNER/REPO.git), check with git remote -v.

  • Create a dedicated SSH key without a passphrase in public/.ssh (id_ed25519) and add its public key to the GitHub repo as a read-only Deploy key. public/.ssh is in .gitignore and is not sent to stations.

  • Create public/.ssh/known_hosts for github.com, then test a pull with the key, as shown in the script comments.

  • Run the watcher as a systemd service so it starts on every boot and restarts if it exits. Use the host user that owns the repo:

    [Unit]
Description=Lente Git Pull Watcher
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=lente
WorkingDirectory=/home/lente/git/scripts
ExecStart=/home/lente/git/scripts/public/git_pull_watcher.sh
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

    Save it as /etc/systemd/system/lente-git-pull-watcher.service, then:

    sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now lente-git-pull-watcher.service

  • Test it by pressing git pull and checking public/.git_pull.log.

Health Checks¶

When enabled/specified in settings.json (see example above) Prism and Lente perform health checks. Each check result is shown in the notification log, at the severity of the first rule that fails.

The disk_space check compares the free disk space against each rule, in order. Prism checks the disk of its result backup folder, Lente checks the disk of its result stage folder, where results from the stations arrive.

  • Prism runs the checks on boot up, when the test configuration changes, and with every ping to Lente. When the severity is Critical Prism does not allow testing to begin.

  • Lente runs the checks on boot up and every 60 seconds. When the severity is Critical Lente refuses result uploads. The stations keep the results staged and send them again once the disk space is fixed, so no results are lost.

  • Prism and Lente report their health in the ping to their Lente, and the Station Manager Health column shows it. Warn is shown in yellow, Error and Critical in red.
